verdict: Notion: Choose Notion when documentation and flexible databases are the primary job, with light project tracking layered on — not as a pure Work OS substitute. Scores use the project-management editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
weaknesses: Can become a messy wiki without standards
Not a Work OS peer on undifferentiated ranks
bestFor: Buyers who want Notion AI writing/search
tradeoffs: Seat minimums and AI credit bundles vs published per-seat floors
Work OS breadth vs specialist timeline / PDF / remote / desktop depth
Automation and reporting depth vs ease of use for small teams
Included AI credits vs paid AI add-ons or credit top-ups
recommendation: Choose Notion when documentation and flexible databases are the primary job, with light project tracking layered on — not as a pure Work OS substitute. Compare Asana/ClickUp/monday for dedicated Work OS execution, Airtable for heavier DB apps, and Jira for engineering delivery.
editorialNotes: Project-management Priority-1 batch. Approved on project-management-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=docs-first. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine project-management editorial criteria using the category weights (work planning 15, automation & workflows 14, ease of use 12, collaboration 12, integrations 12, reporting 10, value 10, scalability 9, AI 6), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — work OS / PM peers, timeline specialists, and adjacent PDF / remote-access / desktop-workspace tools are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
